title: Accelerated degradation of HAP/PLLA bone scaffold by PGA blending facilitates bioactivity and osteoconductivity

nodes.label: Bone scaffolds must degrade with bone growth and stay bioactive; HAP/PLLA degrades slowly and wraps HAP
Blending fast-degrading hydrophilic PGA into HAP/PLLA accelerates degradation, exposes HAP, raising bioactivity and osteoconductivity
HAP nanoneedles in a PLLA matrix as the base bone-scaffold composite
Blend PGA into the PLLA matrix as fast-degrading hydrophilic co-polymer
PLLA:PGA ratio 1:0, 3:1, 1:1, 1:3, 0:1 (1#-5#) at fixed HAP
Laser 3D printing (powder sintering) of composite powders into porous scaffolds
Struts contain crystalline HAP plus PLLA and/or PGA phases, PGA share rising with ratio
Hydrophilicity rises with PGA: water absorption ~430 to ~690%, contact angle ~102 to ~77 deg
Hydrophilic PGA takes up water and hydrolyses fast, opening pores that let fluid attack PLLA
Degradation accelerates with PGA: 4-week PBS weight loss ~3.5% (1#) to ~41% (5#), 3# ~25%
Degradation opens surface pores and cracks and exposes HAP particles, more so with PGA
Exposed HAP dissolves, releasing Ca2+ and PO4 3-; local supersaturation nucleates apatite
Apatite-forming ability in SBF rises with PGA: denser Ca-P deposit layer, Ca/P 1.56 to 1.66
Compressive strength ~16.5 to ~7.5 MPa and modulus ~155 to ~62 MPa fall with PGA
Faster degradation and bioactivity are bought with strength; 1:1 blend balances both
Choose 1PLLA/1PGA/HAP (3#) for cell and in-vivo tests

attrs.reason: moderate strength and degradation, good apatite formation

nodes.label: MG-63 cells adhere, spread and proliferate on 3# over 7 days
Rabbit radius defect with 3#: new bone fills and bridges defect; BV/TV ~52 to ~73% (4-8 wk)

attrs.comparator_claim: more bone than PLLA/HAP and blank (text; qualitative only)

nodes.label: PGA blending accelerates HAP/PLLA scaffold degradation, exposing HAP and improving bioactivity, cytocompatibility and bone repair
Cylindrical scaffold with orthogonal struts and ~500 um interconnected pores

attrs.reason: 100-500 um pores favour cell growth and osteoconduction [34,35]

nodes.label: Printed discs have open orthogonal strut lattice with ~0.5 mm square pores for all compositions
No distinct PLLA/PGA interface in struts, read as good polymer compatibility
SBF deposits are Ca-P with Ca/P 1.56-1.66, called bone-like apatite
PLLA is hydrophobic with low water uptake; PGA hydrophilic with high uptake
Biopolymer degradation exposes wrapped bioceramic to body fluid for ion exchange
Stoichiometric HAP Ca/P = 1.67; also XRD/FTIR band positions: HAP (211) 32 deg, PO4 563 cm-1

attrs.lookup_detail: PLLA 17 deg; PGA (110) 22 deg, (020) 29 deg; OH 3571 cm-1

nodes.label: Top-view photos: regular orthogonal strut lattice with open square pores, colour whitish to beige with PGA

attrs.image_note: Top view only: through-thickness interconnection not visible; pores ~0.5-0.7 mm against the 2 mm bar. PGA/HAP disc is visibly darker (beige) - possible laser discoloration, not discussed. F1b EDS Ca maps do not register onto the SEM powder fields above them (Ca points cover the particle-free background), so the text claim that Ca/P sit in the large particles is not resolvable.

nodes.label: Raw HAP powder: rod-like needles ~100-250 nm long against the 500 nm bar
XRD: PLLA 17 deg and HAP 32 deg peaks in 1#; PGA 22/29 deg rise toward 5#

attrs.image_note: HAP (211) 32 deg reflection is visible only in 1#; in 2#-5# it is lost in noise on the broad amorphous hump, although the text says HAP is presented. PLLA 17 deg peak already gone in 2#.

nodes.label: FTIR: PO4 3- 563 and OH 3571 cm-1 bands in all five scaffolds; C=O, C-O polymer bands

attrs.image_note: PO4/OH bands visible in every trace, so HAP retention across 1#-5# rests on FTIR, not XRD. TGA (F2d) residue ~10-14 wt% at 500 C in all scaffolds is consistent with a retained inorganic fraction.

nodes.label: DSC: separate melting endotherms, PLLA 182 to 174 C and PGA ~215 C, PGA peak growing with ratio

attrs.image_note: Two distinct melting endotherms in 2#-4#: PLLA and PGA crystallise as separate phases (slight PLLA Tm depression suggests only partial interaction); not discussed in the packet text.

nodes.label: Fracture surfaces: smooth stepped in 1#, rougher torn with plastic features toward 5#; no phase boundary

attrs.image_note: SE contrast cannot distinguish PLLA from PGA domains, so absence of a visible interface is weak evidence of compatibility. HAP agglomerate clusters visible on all fracture surfaces (text silent). Brittle-to-tough progression only moderate between a-d.

nodes.label: Compressive strength and modulus bars fall monotonically 1# to 5#; 3# ~12.7 MPa, ~98 MPa

attrs.image_note: F3a stress-strain curves keep the same shape with lower plateau stress as PGA rises.

nodes.label: Water absorption rises monotonically 1# to 5#, ~430 to ~690%
Water contact angle falls monotonically 1# to 5#, ~102 to ~77 deg
PBS weight loss vs time ranks 5#>4#>3#>2#>1# (~41, 36, 25, 15, 3.5% at 4 wk)
Medium pH ~7 for 1# but ~3.2-4.5 for PGA scaffolds (3# ~3.6-4.5) over 4 weeks

attrs.image_note: Strongly acidic degradation medium for all PGA-containing scaffolds including the chosen 3#; apatite nucleation is disfavoured and HAP dissolution favoured at pH ~3.5, and the cell tests do not use degradation-conditioned media. The packet text (truncated) does not reconcile this with apatite deposition or cytocompatibility.

nodes.label: After 28 d PBS: smooth before; fine pores (1#, 2#), cracks (3#, 4#), eroded surface with exposed rods (5#)

attrs.image_note: Exposed particles are clear only on 5# (f); 3# (d), carried forward to biology, shows pores and cracks but no resolved exposed particles. Bright sub-um to ~1.5 um particles are also visible on 1# (b), which the text describes only as tiny pores.

nodes.label: Particles exposed on degraded 5# are ~2-4 um rods and prisms, >10x larger than raw HAP needles

attrs.image_note: F6f rods ~2-4 um long and a few ~3 um prismatic crystals at the crack edge (10 um bar) vs F1a HAP ~100-250 nm. These are not resolved single HAP needles: agglomerates or Ca-P reprecipitated in the acidic medium (F5d pH ~3.2) are equally consistent; no EDS/XRD of the exposed particles.

nodes.label: After 28 d SBF: spherical deposits grow from scattered (1#) to a dense cracked layer (5#)
EDS: Ca, P peaks grow against C, O from 1# to 5#; Ca/P 1.56, 1.63, 1.65, 1.66, 1.66

attrs.image_note: Maximum Ca/P is 1.66, not the stated 1.67. Growth of Ca/P peaks against C/O matches the SEM coverage trend.

nodes.label: EDS Au labels sit on the P K peak (~2 keV) in every spectrum; analysed area not marked

attrs.image_note: Au M (2.12 keV) from the sputter coat overlaps P K (2.01 keV), biasing P and hence Ca/P; spot/area not shown, so exposed HAP filler (Ca/P 1.67 by definition) cannot be separated from new deposit. No XRD/FTIR of the deposit, so "apatite" rests on stoichiometry alone.

nodes.label: Calcein-stained MG-63 cells elongated with filopodia; live-cell density rises from 1 to 7 d

attrs.image_note: One dead (red) cell at 5 d; confluent by 5-7 d. No scaffold struts visible in the field; only 3# tested, no control scaffold.

nodes.label: SEM: polygonal cells spread with interconnected filopodia, covering the surface by 7 d

attrs.image_note: Scaffold surface cracks visible beneath cells at 1-5 d.

nodes.label: CCK-8 absorbance rises ~0.43 to ~1.94 from day 1 to day 7 on 3#
X-ray radiographs: defect zones (dashed) gain radiopacity from 4 to 8 wk in all three groups

attrs.image_note: Columns are not labelled with group names; between-group difference in radiopacity is not evident.

nodes.label: Micro-CT renders of three unlabelled groups show no evident between-group difference in defect filling

attrs.image_note: Defects partly filled at 4 wk and cortex more continuous at 8 wk in all columns; columns carry no group labels (text order 3#, PLLA/HAP, blank assumed). With BV/TV and BMD given only for 3# (F9 bars), the text claim of more bone than PLLA/HAP and blank has neither visual nor quantitative support.

nodes.label: HE and MT sections of 3#: fibrous and new bone tissue at 4 wk, denser mineralised matrix at 8 wk

attrs.image_note: Histology only for 3#; vessels are not identifiable at this magnification.

nodes.label: 3# only: BV/TV ~52 to ~73% and BMD ~205 to ~310 mg/cc from 4 to 8 wk

attrs.image_note: Bars exist only for 3#; no PLLA/HAP or blank values, so the text claim of more bone than the controls has no quantitative support.

notes: Spine: need -> PGA-blending hypothesis -> HAP/PLLA base + PGA + ratio sweep -> laser printing -> blended phases with HAP retained (XRD+FTIR+DSC) -> hydrophilicity -> hydrolytic degradation -> HAP exposure -> apatite formation, against a strength loss (second branch) meeting at the trade-off -> down-select 3# -> cytocompatibility -> in-vivo repair -> conclusion. Lost: TGA, stress-strain shapes, powder SEM/EDS (F1b maps do not register onto SEM fields), fracture-mode change, and the DSC evidence that PLLA and PGA crystallise separately (kept as image_note on o6; it weakens the side claim s2 of 'no interface'). The degradation->bioactivity link is correlational across one PGA series (o8/o10 correlate_across_series), and the image audits cut it at the chosen composition: F6 shows exposed particles clearly only on 5#, and those are 2-4 um rods (a1) >10x the raw HAP needles; apatite identity rests on EDS stoichiometry with an Au/P overlap (a2); media reach pH ~3.5 (o11), which works against apatite nucleation and is untested on cells. Cell and in-vivo tests use 3# only with no in-vitro control and no quantified control groups (o22), so the conclusion's comparative claims on cytocompatibility and bone repair are argued rather than measured.
